content_of_post_to_comment: Self-improvement isn't about finding more motivation. It's about getting rid of the daily negotiation you have with your willpower. There is no winning in negotiating with yourself. You know all your weak-points and as soon as you start negotiating with yourself you have already lost. Instead, get rid of the decision so you don't have to negotiate with yourself. Instead of decision paralysis about what to eat for dinner, have pre-made meals ready so that it is easier to eat at home than to go eat out (if only because you don't have to pick from which of the 5 places you go to you're the least tired of that day). Easy principle, but it applies through many areas of your life. Keep a pair of walking shoes in the car so you can still go walk even if your appointment ran long and you're far from home. Keep healthy snacks in the car so that you don't pig out at the candy aisle if you are away from home.
comment: The walking shoes in the car example is such a practical way to think about it. I've noticed a lot of habits fail because the "right" choice requires extra effort at the exact moment we're tired or stressed. Removing those tiny decisions ahead of time seems less about discipline and more about making the default option work in your favor.
